clue.text: Question framed by a leading lady?

definitions.text: Question framed by a leading lady?

parts.words: Question framed by a leading lady?
parts.note: surface reading: some query posed by the star actress of a show
setter's reading: the heroine of Shakespeare's tragedy, Juliet, who asks a famous question from her balcony about Romeo's surname

explanation.surface: An interviewer wonders what question the star actress might pose.
explanation.walkthrough: Juliet, the title heroine of Romeo and Juliet, asks this on her balcony; the rest of the line is 'that which we call a rose...'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the actual question Juliet speaks in Shakespeare's play, so it is literally a query posed by a leading female role.

clue.text: Why old men all scratch their bottoms around Spain? It's unrefined

indicators.note: the trimmed words are placed round the country abbreviation, enclosing it
to scratch the bottom of each word is to rub out its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about why elderly men scratch their backsides in Spain, with an aside that it's crude.
explanation.walkthrough: Each of the four words loses its last letter, and the Spain letter sits between the second and third of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Wholemeal flour keeps the whole grain, bran included, so it is not refined like white flour.

clue.text: Fish starter's off the menu for Mr & Mrs

indicators.note: the first item on the list goes, so the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: Mr is the title for a man
Mrs is the title of a married woman

explanation.surface: A married couple find the fish starter has been taken off the menu.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr and Mrs give a male and a wife; the first letter of the whole pair goes.
explanation.definitionFit: The alewife is a North American herring-like fish, so it is an example of a fish.

clue.text: Plastic bags covering up a bit of brewer's droop

indicators.note: plastic material can be moulded into any shape, so the letters are remoulded
covering something up hides it from view, so that letter disappears

parts.note: taken as written
the opening letter of brewer's

explanation.surface: Plastic bags hide the embarrassing effect of too much beer, known as brewer's droop.
explanation.walkthrough: Brewer's droop is British slang for drink-induced impotence, but only 'droop' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To sag is to hang down or sink under weight, the same as a droop.

clue.text: Rising star accepts Lethal Weapon but not Fifty Shades

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so one piece goes inside the other
in a down clue, rising means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Sun is a star

indicators.note: excluding something from a word means taking those letters out

parts.note: a lance is a deadly weapon
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A rising film star takes an action blockbuster role but turns down an erotic one.
explanation.walkthrough: Lethal Weapon and Fifty Shades look like film titles, but the first is a lance and 'Shades' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shades are subtle gradations of colour or meaning, which is what nuances are.

clue.text: See 1
Arsenal finishing second and losing league here?

definitions.text: Arsenal finishing second and losing league here?

indicators.note: to finish something off is to kill it, so the letter for second is removed
a word that loses something has those letters taken away

parts.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for second
L is the abbreviation for league

explanation.surface: Arsenal, the London football club, come second and miss out on the league title.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue asks where such a defeat would happen: in a sports stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a stadium or venue where teams compete, so it is where a club would finish second.

clue.text: Thus Spake Zarathustra gave standards about it

indicators.note: the words have the solution about them, wrapping it inside their run of letters

parts.note: the run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: Nietzsche's book in which the prophet Zarathustra lays down moral standards.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: it names the language in which the real Zarathustra (Zoroaster) spoke.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Iranian language of the Zoroastrian scriptures is what the prophet Zoroaster himself used.

clue.text: Part of Benedictine order

indicators.note: only a portion of the following word's letters is wanted

parts.note: letters two to six of the word

explanation.surface: A section of the Benedictine monastic order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a religious order but is a command.
explanation.definitionFit: A decree or command issued by authority is an order, in its sense of an instruction.

clue.text: Securing final in tennis, Wade's opponent climbed rankings

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast, so one piece goes around another

parts.note: Roe v Wade was the US Supreme Court abortion case

indicators.note: the final letter of the word that follows is the one kept

parts.note: the last letter of tennis

explanation.surface: A tennis player wins the final against someone called Wade and moves up the rankings.
explanation.walkthrough: Wade suggests Virginia Wade the tennis player, but here it is the defendant in Roe v Wade.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose is the past tense of rise, and to rise is to climb, so it matches climbed.

clue.text: German people displaying magnanimity

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for German
a race is a people

explanation.surface: Germans showing generosity of spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Graciousness or generosity of spirit towards others is a kind of magnanimity.

clue.text: Retrospective name associated with Ireland

indicators.note: looking back means the letters are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for name
Ire is short for Ireland (Éire)

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned name linked with Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken as a whole, the clue also defines the answer: an old poetic name for Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the poetic, old-fashioned name for the island, so it is a nostalgic name tied to it.

clue.text: Pretty — possessed of sex appeal in truth

indicators.note: to be possessed of something is to hold it, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: pretty as in 'pretty good', meaning very
'it' is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: Someone pretty who truly has sex appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pretty' looks like an adjective but is used as an adverb.
explanation.definitionFit: A verity is a true principle or fact, so the word is a formal synonym for truth.

clue.text: Desperately hope for New Age to come earlier

indicators.note: the second item is told to be placed first rather than in clue order

parts.note: a year is an age, as in 'it took years'
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Desperately hoping for a New Age to arrive sooner.
explanation.definitionFit: To long or ache for something is to wish desperately to have it.

clue.text: Virtue of reduced speed in built-up area

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a city is a built-up area

indicators.note: a reduced word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: haste is speed

explanation.surface: Slowing down in town is a virtue for drivers.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like road safety advice on speed limits.
explanation.definitionFit: Sexual abstinence was traditionally counted among the Christian virtues, so it is an example of one.

clue.text: Dolly maybe getting 50% bosom reduction a day earlier

indicators.note: the middle letter is cut to half of itself, double-u becoming a single vee

parts.note: Dolly was the famous cloned sheep

explanation.surface: Dolly Parton, perhaps, having breast reduction surgery the day before.
explanation.walkthrough: W is written as two Vs, so halving the middle letter leaves V; 'bosom' means the middle of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: The evening or day before an event, as in Christmas Eve, is the day earlier.

clue.text: Banks of huge river in Russia's state capital

indicators.note: the banks are the two edges, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: the first and last letters of huge
the Lena is a great Siberian river

explanation.surface: The banks of a vast Russian river, and that country's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russia's state capital' suggests Moscow; the capital is in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: this mining-boom town became the seat of government for Montana in the American West.

clue.text: Boundless sand outside of Nigeria in semi-wild, hot biome

indicators.note: the selected letters go inside the outer pieces
semi means half, so only half of the word is kept

parts.note: savage means wild
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: without its bounds, the word keeps only its inner letters

parts.note: the middle letters of sand

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of Nigeria

explanation.surface: Endless sand around Nigeria in a half-wild, hot landscape.
explanation.walkthrough: The two pairs of selected letters sit between the first half of the wild word and the hot letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A grassland ecosystem with scattered trees, typical of tropical Africa, is a recognised biome.

clue.text: Very good to adopt feminine principle in competition

indicators.note: adopting something takes it in, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very
G is the abbreviation for good
yin is the feminine principle in Chinese philosophy

explanation.surface: It is very good to embrace femininity in competitive situations.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone competing against rivals is contending with them, which is the participle meaning in competition.

clue.text: Piece of engineering close to Santa Fe bridging rocky glen

indicators.note: a bridge spans a gap, so the outer pieces sit on either side of the inner
rocky means unsteady, so the letters are shaken into a new order
the close of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the last letter of Santa
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
taken as written

explanation.surface: An engineering structure near Santa Fe spans a rocky valley.
explanation.walkthrough: Santa Fe reads as the New Mexico city, but Fe is the symbol for a metal.
explanation.definitionFit: A steel bar with an L-shaped cross-section is a standard structural component used in engineering.

clue.text: Barrier protecting both sides around old Renaissance city

indicators.note: something protected is enclosed and shielded by what surrounds it

parts.note: a fence is a barrier

indicators.note: these letters sit round the next piece

parts.note: L and R, left and right
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A defensive wall surrounding an old Renaissance town.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tuscan city was the cradle of the Italian Renaissance, home to the Medici and Michelangelo.

clue.text: Habit of organist's regularly entertaining pieces

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to take them in, so one piece goes inside
taking letters at regular intervals means every other one

parts.note: the second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters
chess pieces are called men

explanation.surface: An organist's routine of regularly playing pieces for an audience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' suggests a routine, but here it is a nun's or monk's clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a garment such as a monk wears, and the answer is a literary word for clothing.

clue.text: Sort of nemeses endlessly besieging one?

definitions.text: Sort of nemeses endlessly besieging one?

indicators.note: an army besieging a town surrounds it, so these letters go round the next
to sort letters is to arrange them afresh
with no end, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Some kind of arch-rivals laying siege to a person.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, the clue describes the answer: foes surrounding someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Foes who surround and attack a person are hostile opponents, a kind of nemesis.

clue.text: Righteous anger after nation's exported zero dyestuff

indicators.note: something exported is sent out of the country, so those letters leave the word

parts.note: indignation is anger at unfairness
taken as written
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: Outrage after a country exports none of its dyes.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep blue dye originally obtained from plants is one of the classic natural dyestuffs.

clue.text: Backed up bog blocks means of access down the drain

indicators.note: something blocking a gap sits inside it

parts.note: a door is how you get in

indicators.note: in a down clue, backed up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a fen is a bog

explanation.surface: A blocked toilet backs up and stops the plumbing from draining.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bog' is British slang for toilet, which drives the plumbing picture, but here it means marshland.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms for something ruined or lost beyond saving.

clue.text: Bread and butter free from New York

indicators.note: a word free from something no longer contains those letters

parts.note: a butter is something that butts, such as a nanny goat
NY is the abbreviation for New York

explanation.surface: Bread and butter without additives, from New York.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread and butter' looks like a pair, but 'butter' is an animal that butts.
explanation.definitionFit: Naan is a leavened flatbread from South Asian cooking, an example of bread.

clue.text: Job's quality created by 1 in 10 falling into step

indicators.note: the first number goes inside the second

parts.note: a pace is a step

indicators.note: falling into something puts you inside it

parts.note: the number written as a word
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A quality achieved when one in ten people falls into line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Job' looks like work, but it is the biblical Job, famous for enduring suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical Job endured terrible trials without cursing God, so his proverbial virtue is long-suffering endurance.

clue.text: It's sad for Romeo, a knave Juliet's left

parts.note: taken as written
the knave is the jack in a pack of cards
Juliet is J in the NATO alphabet
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: Romeo laments that Juliet has gone off with a scoundrel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Juliet's left' means J has become L: the J of the card is swapped for L.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an archaic exclamation of sorrow, the sort of word Romeo would cry in Shakespeare's English.

clue.text: "How's your father?" is in noisy exchanges with "All right!"

indicators.note: exchanging one thing with another swaps them in place

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
OK means all right

explanation.surface: Someone asks after a father and gets a loud chorus of 'All right!' back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How's your father' is British slang for sex, not a polite enquiry; the two letters of 'is' inside the noisy word are swapped for the all-right letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are cheeky British colloquialisms for sexual activity, so they are slang synonyms.

clue.text: Red-headed queen on horse keeping fashionable

indicators.note: keeping something means holding it inside

parts.note: gee-gee is a childish word for horse
in means fashionable
ER is the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth

explanation.surface: A red-haired queen rides a horse, staying stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' places the queen after the horse in an across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair of an orange-red colour is called by this spice name, especially in Britain.

clue.text: Grow weary of dear Juliet, broken without Romeo

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, ready to be put back in another order
without something means with those letters left out

parts.note: taken as written
Juliet is J in the NATO alphabet
Romeo is R in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: Dear Juliet tires, heartbroken without Romeo.
explanation.walkthrough: Romeo and Juliet are the lovers on the surface but just R and J here.
explanation.definitionFit: To jade is to tire or wear out, so someone jaded has grown weary of something.

clue.text: Take back Wicked Oscar for one with green skin?

indicators.note: taking words back means reading them in the opposite direction

parts.note: evil means wicked
Oscar is O in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: An Oscar is reclaimed from the musical Wicked, whose heroine is the green-skinned Elphaba.
explanation.walkthrough: Wicked is the musical about a green witch, which is why 'green skin' feels like part of the show.
explanation.definitionFit: Many olives have green skin when picked, so the question mark marks a fruit as the green-skinned one.

clue.text: Overnight cobbler of the German football team

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a little helper in the fairy tale who makes shoes while the shoemaker sleeps
second meaning: the German word for eleven, the number in a football side

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a German team's shoe repairer; it is really a Grimm tale and a German number.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Elves and the Shoemaker the tiny creatures make shoes by night, and German for eleven matches a full football side.

clue.text: Symbol for elite rugby nations' leaders?

definitions.text: Symbol for elite rugby nations' leaders?

indicators.note: the leaders of words are their opening letters

parts.note: the first letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: An emblem used by the top teams of the rugby world.
explanation.walkthrough: Read whole, the clue is the definition: the silver plant is New Zealand's rugby emblem, worn by the All Blacks.
explanation.definitionFit: The silver one is the national emblem of New Zealand, worn by its elite All Blacks rugby side.

clue.text: Tackle temporarily emptied pool

parts.note: tackle is equipment, kit

indicators.note: an emptied word has its contents gone, keeping only the outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of temporarily

explanation.surface: Fishing tackle left beside a pool that has been drained for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pool' suggests water, but it is a shared fund of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A pool is a shared fund of money that a group contributes to, as is a kitty.

clue.text: Dark Lord gets very loud replacement for Posh Spice

indicators.note: one item is put in place of another, swapping it out

parts.note: Sauron is the Dark Lord of The Lord of the Rings
fortissimo, very loud in music
U means upper-class, posh

explanation.surface: A villain loudly replaces Posh Spice of the Spice Girls.
explanation.walkthrough: Posh Spice was Victoria Beckham's Spice Girls name; here Posh is U and Spice alone the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The dried stigmas of a crocus are sold as a costly cooking spice.
